key_provisions_or_claims: Congress should preempt burdensome state AI laws to create a minimally burdensome national standard, with carve-outs for generally applicable state laws, zoning and state procurement.
Protect children via age assurance, parental controls and features reducing sexual exploitation and self-harm risks.
Create regulatory sandboxes and no new federal AI rulemaking body; rely on existing sector regulators and industry-led standards.
Leave AI training on copyrighted material to the courts; consider licensing frameworks and a federal digital replica right.
Protect residential ratepayers from data center costs while streamlining permitting for AI infrastructure.
annotation.summary_en: White House legislative recommendations (March 2026) for a national AI policy framework: child protection, communities and energy costs, IP, anti-censorship, innovation via sandboxes, workforce, and federal preemption of burdensome state AI laws. Opposes a new federal AI regulator, favoring existing agencies and industry-led standards.
annotation.title_clean: A National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence: Legislative Recommendations
